issues.t: Brakes may briefly lose pressure at low speed (recall)
issues.sym: During light braking in a turn, or when a wheel hits a bump such as a driveway lip, the brakes can briefly lose pressure and the car doesn't slow as expected. Braking returns on the next pedal press.
issues.why: Brake control software can misjudge wheel slip after the brakes are released and reapplied for a moment, and briefly cut braking. The recall covers Blazer EV SS and police versions along with several Cadillac EVs.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 26V-717. Accept the free over-the-air update or have a dealer install it. Until then, leave extra distance when braking over bumps and in turns.

issues.t: Parking brake may apply or fail from harness damage (recall)
issues.sym: Parking brake warnings, the parking brake setting itself while driving, or the parking brake not holding when parked.
issues.why: The wiring harness for the rear electric parking brake can rub through or corrode. Some cars repaired under the first recall were not fixed correctly and were recalled again.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 25V-433 and 26V-031. Dealers inspect, reroute and tape the harness, or replace it if damaged, for free.

issues.t: Right front lower control arm may crack (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking or wandering from the front, or in the worst case a sudden loss of steering control.
issues.why: A manufacturing defect in the right front lower control arm on some 2024 cars could cause it to fracture.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 24V-487. Dealers inspect and replace the arm free as needed.

issues.t: Rear drive motor wiring may short, loss of power (recall)
issues.sym: A warning message and sudden loss of drive power while driving.
issues.why: Wires inside the rear drive motor on a small number of 2024 cars were not insulated well enough and could touch and short out.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 24V-320. Dealers replace the rear drive unit free.

issues.sym: A door that doesn't latch firmly or could pop open while driving.
issues.why: Some door strikers (the U-shaped catch on the door frame) were not heat-treated properly and can crack. Recalls covered a small number of 2024 and 2025 cars.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 23V-869 and 24V-737. Dealers replace all four door strikers free.

issues.t: Early software faults: dead screens, charging and battery warnings
issues.sym: Many problems at once on early cars: screens freezing or going black, high-voltage battery warnings, refusing to charge or failed DC fast charging, glitchy window switches and navigation, and in some cases reduced power.
issues.why: GM paused Blazer EV sales in December 2023 to fix what it called software quality issues across many control modules. GM said the problems were not related to the Ultium battery itself.
issues.next: Make sure every GM software campaign for your VIN has been done. A dealer with EV-certified technicians can check; the full update can take hours or a day.

issues.t: Service High Voltage message with dead 12-volt battery
issues.sym: The check engine light or a Service High Voltage message comes on, and the 12-volt battery may go flat now and then, leaving the car unable to start.
issues.why: GM bulletin PIP6021 blames a software problem in the battery energy control module that wrongly flags the battery's cell monitoring units, setting a group of battery communication codes. The false fault can also keep the car's computers awake and drain the 12-volt battery.
issues.next: Have a Chevrolet EV dealer check for the codes in bulletin PIP6021, update the battery control module software and run GM's reset steps. Accept future over-the-air updates.

issues.t: Service High Voltage warning from battery software codes
issues.sym: A Service High Voltage message and check engine light, often with no change in how the car drives.
issues.why: GM bulletin PIT6044M lists a software anomaly that sets high-voltage battery communication codes (U2220 to U2237 or U2C11) across its Ultium EVs.
issues.next: A dealer should first save the battery data GM asks for, then update the battery control module software and do the reset steps in the bulletin. If codes come back, GM's technical team gets involved.

issues.t: No cabin heat with Service High Voltage warning
issues.sym: The heater blows cold and a Service High Voltage warning appears, with code P1C01 stored.
issues.why: GM bulletin 25-NA-067 says the cause may be software anomalies in the battery energy control module, which also manages the system that heats the cabin and battery.
issues.next: Ask a dealer about bulletin 25-NA-067. The fix is a software update to the battery control module; no parts should need replacing.

issues.t: Wiring harness rubs on front axle, charging limited to 26%
issues.sym: A high-voltage system message with the check engine light on, and the car will only charge to about 26%.
issues.why: In the front motor area, a low-voltage wiring harness running to the A/C compressor can rub against the right front axle shaft until the wires chafe through (GM bulletin PIC6609).
issues.next: Have a dealer inspect the harness near the right front axle and CV boot clamp. Chafed wires are spliced and the harness is rerouted and clipped properly.

issues.t: Unable to charge or DC fast charging unavailable
issues.sym: An Unable to Charge or Service High Voltage message, or a check engine light, and DC fast chargers won't work even though home charging may still work.
issues.why: GM bulletin PIP5994A ties code P2980 to several causes: a software anomaly, snow, ice or moisture in the charge port, plugging in while the car is not in Park, or a real high-voltage insulation fault.
issues.next: Make sure the car is in Park before plugging in and keep the port clean and dry. If the message stays, a dealer should check the code and insulation readings and install the newer software.

issues.t: Touchscreen or gauge display goes black or reboots
issues.sym: The center screen or driver display flickers, goes black and comes back, or reboots while driving. CarPlay, Android Auto, Bluetooth, audio, camera or climate controls can also act up.
issues.why: GM's bulletins (PIT6362 and PIT6393 series) put most of these down to software, with some loose display cable connections. GM tells dealers not to replace the radio for most of these symptoms.
issues.next: Install all over-the-air updates and keep your phone updated. If a screen stays black, a dealer can reset the radio, update software and check the display cables.

issues.t: False low 12-volt battery alerts from OnStar
issues.sym: You get OnStar emails saying the 12-volt battery is low and to visit a dealer, but the car works normally.
issues.why: A software error in the body control module made OnStar think the battery voltage was low (GM bulletin 25-NA-048).
issues.next: If the car starts and runs normally, ask a dealer to confirm the body control module has software 24.25.173 or later. No battery charging or replacement is needed for this alert alone.

issues.t: Service Brake System warning and loss of brake assist
issues.sym: A chime and Service Brake System message with ABS, traction and brake lights on, a hard brake pedal, and top speed limited to about 43 mph. Some drivers report losing brake assist while braking.
issues.why: NHTSA opened investigation EA26006 into the eBoost brake-by-wire unit used on many GM vehicles including this one. GM points to a fracture of a spindle inside the unit. No recall has been announced yet.
issues.next: If the warning appears, slow down, leave extra stopping distance and press the pedal firmly. Get the car to a dealer, towing it if braking feels weak, and watch for a recall on your VIN.
